clue.text: Weak case made for charitable collection

parts.note: a poor argument or effort is a weak one
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: Someone builds a flimsy argument in support of a charity appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor box is the alms box in a church where coins for the needy are dropped, a collection for charity.

clue.text: Love to appear in costume but has no chance

indicators.note: the love letter is to appear in the middle of the costume word, so it is placed inside

parts.note: an outfit is a costume or set of clothes
love is nil in tennis, the round letter O

explanation.surface: An actor longs to be cast in a costume role but is told the part is beyond reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, read as 'is out of it': no longer in contention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of it is an idiom for being out of contention, with no hope of winning.

clue.text: Limits area where cattle may graze

definitions.meaning: the ... of something is its scope, the limits it reaches between
open grazing land, especially in the American West

explanation.surface: A rancher sets boundaries on the grassland where the herd may feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the extent or bounds of something and the open land where livestock roam and feed.

clue.text: Popped the question after work but not accepted

indicators.note: the posing comes after the work in the clue, so the work piece goes first

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to pose a question is to put it, so 'popped the question' gives posed

explanation.surface: A man proposed marriage after a day at work, only to be turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popped the question' looks like a marriage proposal but just means asked, posed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opposed has been resisted or rejected, so it was not accepted.

clue.text: It will result in a free kick for the away team

definitions.text: It will result in a free kick for the away team

parts.words: It will result in a free kick for the away team
parts.note: in football an offence of being beyond the defence gives the other side a free kick

explanation.surface: A football referee's decision hands the visitors a set piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The away team is the side that is off, away from home, which gives a second reading of the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught ahead of the last defender in football is penalised with an indirect free kick to the opponents.

clue.text: Work in a band in fraudulent transaction

definitions.meaning: a violin, the instrument played in a folk or country band, is informally called this
a swindle or dishonest piece of trickery, such as cooked accounts

explanation.surface: A musician's gig with a group turns out to be cover for a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the informal name of a violin played in bands and slang for a swindle.

clue.text: He has found a job at last

definitions.text: He has found a job at last

parts.words: He has found a job at last
parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler works on, so his job is literally done at a last

explanation.surface: A long-unemployed man finally gets hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally', but a last is the wooden foot model used by a cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler who makes footwear does his work on a last, the wooden form shaped like a foot.

clue.text: Retired from employment?

parts.note: 'employment' here means use: something taken out of use has been retired from service

explanation.surface: A question about someone who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests a pensioner, but the employment is that of an object being used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer used, like a closed railway line, has been withdrawn from service.

clue.text: Enthusiastic recommendation, which is unique

definitions.meaning: a phrase of glowing praise, as in 'there's no better'
said of something matchless, with no equal anywhere

explanation.surface: A reviewer heaps praise on something one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used both to praise something as the best and to say nothing else resembles it.

clue.text: Heads turn in shock

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the word for heads the other way round

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads, as in 'off one's nut'

explanation.surface: People's heads swivel in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or daze them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Immodest assertion one isn't ashamed to make

definitions.text: Immodest assertion one isn't ashamed to make

parts.words: Immodest assertion one isn't ashamed to make
parts.note: a boastful claim made with pride, proud being the opposite of ashamed

explanation.surface: Someone brags shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A boast is an immodest claim, and making it proudly means feeling no shame about it.

clue.text: Proposals for heartless transgressors

indicators.note: heartless asks for the central letters of the word for transgressors to be cut out

parts.note: offenders are people who transgress, breaking a law or rule

explanation.surface: Plea deals are put to cruel criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes END, the three middle letters of OFFENDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Offers are proposals or bids put forward for acceptance.

clue.text: Position of respect on the staff

definitions.text: Position of respect on the staff

parts.words: Position of respect on the staff
parts.note: the staff is a flagpole, and a flag lowered part way down it marks mourning

explanation.surface: A senior employee holds a respected post in the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is the pole a flag flies from.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags are lowered partway down the pole as a mark of respect after a death.

clue.text: Servant, a sober worker, receives tip

indicators.note: the string formed from a, sober and worker takes in the tip, which sits inside it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a sober abstainer
an ant is the classic worker insect
an end is a tip or extremity

explanation.surface: A teetotal household worker accepts a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a gratuity given to a servant, but it means an extremity; 'receives' puts it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant is someone who waits on or serves another, a servant.

clue.text: Sort of church Alice pops out to see

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Alice nips out to visit the cathedral of her bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' scrambles ALICE POPS. A see is a bishop's diocese, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An Episcopal church is one governed by bishops, such as the Anglican church in the USA.

clue.text: Accidentally slips a little butter on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts something inside the steamship letters

parts.note: on board conventionally means inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship
a kid is a young goat, a small creature that butts

explanation.surface: Someone drops a smear of butter on the deck or a chopping board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread but something that butts, a young goat; 'on board' is the convention for going inside the steamship letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To skid is to slide out of control by accident, losing grip.

clue.text: Confess one's escaped from Maidstone somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters come out in some new order

parts.note: the letters of one's are what escape from the town name

explanation.surface: A prisoner has broken out of a Kentish jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escaped from' takes O, N, E and S out of MAIDSTONE (a town in Kent, home to a prison), and the leftover MAIDT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess or own up to it.

clue.text: Fishing boat that will sail with the tide

definitions.meaning: a vessel using drift nets, especially for herring

definitions.text: that will sail with the tide
definitions.meaning: something carried along by the current without steering, a wanderer

explanation.surface: A trawler sets off when the tide turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a drift-net fishing vessel and anything or anyone carried passively by currents.

clue.text: Package returned, give address with added detail

indicators.note: returned sends the word for package back the other way

parts.note: a bale is a large bound package, as of hay or cotton
to orate is to deliver a formal speech or address

explanation.surface: A parcel is sent back and someone fills in the delivery address more fully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give address' looks like writing on a parcel but means make a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate, worked out with many details.

clue.text: Home fixture for City but needs to be arranged

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: arranged tells us the little word but is put into a different order

explanation.surface: A football club called City needs a home game scheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home fixture' sounds like a football match, but it is an installation in a house. BATH is an English city, and its football club is Bath City.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub fitted in the bathroom is literally a fixture in a home.

clue.text: Much of his time is spent behind bars

definitions.text: Much of his time is spent behind bars

parts.words: Much of his time is spent behind bars
parts.note: the bars are pub counters, and someone who draws beer works behind them

explanation.surface: A habitual criminal who keeps going back to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests prison, but here they are the counters of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster draws and serves beer, so he works behind the bar of an inn.

clue.text: Skin disease going around English riding school

indicators.note: the skin complaint goes around the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: mange is a skin disease of animals caused by mites

explanation.surface: An outbreak of skin complaints spreads through a stable of English horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A manege is an enclosed arena where horses and riders are trained in dressage.

clue.text: Poorly made Russian fighter returns with a bang!

indicators.note: returns has the name of the Russian jet coming back the other way

parts.note: the MiG is a famous Russian fighter aircraft
a crack is a sudden sharp bang

explanation.surface: A jet fighter comes home, breaking the sound barrier noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes things flimsy and shoddily made, showy but cheap.

clue.text: Hits the first bumps

indicators.note: the first means just the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: humps are bumps or rounded swellings

explanation.surface: A car hits the opening speed bumps on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumps are heavy blows, so hits in the sense of strikes.

clue.text: Consumers requiring faultless service in US

indicators.note: in places the shortened service inside the two letters of US

parts.note: the US letters are taken as written

indicators.note: faultless takes away the fault, a vice, from the word service

explanation.surface: American customers expect impeccable service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faultless' looks like praise, but it removes VICE (a fault) from SERVICE, leaving SER.
explanation.definitionFit: Users are consumers, people who use up a product or service.

clue.text: Side plate put out, with tin-opener, for basic food

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and reordered

parts.note: the opener of the word tin is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: Someone lays a side plate and fetches a can opener before a simple meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin-opener' is not a kitchen tool but the opening letter of 'tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple diet is the food someone eats regularly as the basis of their meals.

clue.text: Dines in style at smart restaurants

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone dines in style at fashionable restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is a plain synonym of dines, taking a meal.

clue.text: Girl, being awkward, went ahead and asked questions

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of girl are twisted out of shape

parts.note: someone who went ahead of others led them

explanation.surface: A difficult girl pushes forward and starts quizzing people.
explanation.definitionFit: To be grilled is to be questioned closely, so grilled means interrogated.

clue.text: They take advantage of a sailor needing employers

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
those who employ something, in the sense of use it, are users

explanation.surface: Exploiters take advantage of a seaman who needs work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employers' means people who employ, or use, things, not bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusers exploit others, misusing them for their own gain.
